tables.purpose: The observation authority and its own query engine: immutable OBS# observation revisions, the per-scope accepted frontier and deletion fence, the accepted- and event-time segment directories, staged admission pages and their receipts, the durable spool and usage outbox, series claims and their cardinality counters, workspace ingest quota, the regional ingress gate, telemetry gaps, export state and export checkpoints. There is no downstream projection store and no change-feed rail: this table answers every supported query shape itself.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Per-authority customer managed key. Observation rows carry customer log bodies and span attributes inline, so they may not share a key with any other authority.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_scope_time
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Scope-ordered event time. Only observation revisions carry tPk, so no control row, receipt or spool chunk can appear in a scope listing. The partition carries the signal, the event-time hour bucket and the shard, so a walk is a bounded range read per bucket rather than a scan.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_ws_accepted
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Workspace-ordered accepted time, tie-broken by an eight-hex scope digest so cross-session ordering needs no shared counter. Same slim projection as the other dense indexes: attrS, attrN and attrB are deliberately absent, so a page that needs customer attributes issues a base-table BatchGetItem instead of tripling retained bytes.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_ws_time
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Workspace-ordered event time, the axis a dashboard reads. It is a separate index from the accepted-time one because a query may not silently answer an event-time question from an accepted-time order.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_metric
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: One exact metric name inside one workspace per UTC day. KEYS_ONLY: an aggregate reads points from the base table under an explicit scan bound, so the index cannot become a second, unbounded copy of the series.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_trace
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: One trace inside one scope, ordered by signal rank. KEYS_ONLY: only spans and logs carrying a traceId appear, and the spans themselves are read by key from the base table.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_control
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: The reconciler and the export launcher scan due work by domain shard and due time. KEYS_ONLY is what keeps the launcher's grant free of any observation read: a due page carries keys, and the launcher never sees a record.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_gap
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Workspace-scoped gap listing; a session-scoped gap query reads the base table by key. Only gap revisions carry gwPk, and the projection carries the gap's own fields and no observation field at all.

stream.rationale: A wake is a hint and carries no payload; KEYS_ONLY makes that structural, because there are no bytes to emit even by mistake. Frame bytes always come from a strongly consistent base-table range read at the socket's own durable position, so a missed, duplicated or reordered wake changes latency only.

timeToLive.rationale: Every reclaimable family here is reclaimed by a fenced reconciler duty that proves its own progress: batch.expire retires a preparing receipt past its deadline, spool.repair redrives an unacknowledged chunk, series.reclaim releases an idle claim against its counter in one transaction, and deletion.execute removes observations under a pinned deletion epoch. A TTL delete is unordered, unfenced and invisible to those duties, so it could remove a staged page mid-commit or a claim the counter still counts.

tables.purpose: Read-only regional projection of workspace placement, descriptive profiles, effective limits, API key revocation and the signed feed frontier. Written only by central-control-worker; every regional role holds GetItem and Query and nothing else. The item shapes are assumed by the regional stream and must be confirmed by the central stream (G-3).

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Per-authority customer managed key. The projection carries authorization epochs, not credentials.

stream.rationale: The projection is a read replica of central control state; regional consumers read it by key, never by change feed.

timeToLive.rationale: A revocation row that silently disappeared would fail open, which is the one direction this table must never fail.

tables.purpose: Content body descriptors, inline ciphertext bodies, Merkle tree pages, root descriptors, root and body pins, download grants, GC epochs and GC candidates. Every partition is workspace scoped.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: A dedicated content CMK, distinct from every other regional table (R-SECRETS). The key policy requires kms:EncryptionContext:aex:workspace to equal the caller workspace on Encrypt, Decrypt and GenerateDataKey (OD-18).

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_gc
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: One index serves both mark (enumerate every body and page in 256 bounded buckets per workspace) and sweep (enumerate candidates). There is deliberately no reverse owner index and no reference count (R-DELETE): pin removal is a DeleteItem on a known key.

stream.rationale: KEYS_ONLY because the table holds ciphertext bodies; a NEW_IMAGE stream would duplicate every inline body into stream storage and into the pipe role blast radius. Storage usage facts ride regional-work transactionally instead.

timeToLive.rationale: Grant pins and grant state rows only, at expiry plus a 3600 second grace. GC never trusts it: GC re-reads expiresAt and refuses to delete a body whose grant pin has not provably expired.

tables.purpose: The current (workspace, kind, name) registry pointer with its revision and ETag, multipart upload staging rows, and registry idempotency receipts.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Per-authority customer managed key. The registry stores pointers and digests, never bodies.

stream.rationale: D-22: pointer replacement stages the previous content for GC through a cross-table transaction with regional-content, so no stream consumer is needed.

timeToLive.rationale: Receipts only (OD-16, 24 hours). Upload rows deliberately have no TTL: a TTL deletion would orphan the live S3 multipart upload, and the 24-hour sweeper must abort the upload before removing the row.

tables.purpose: Workspace secret metadata, hidden source generations carrying ciphertext, session custody heads and bindings, the revocation epoch, managed-call authorizations, the provider-credential binding directory for BYOK, and the per-session redaction digest manifest.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: A dedicated secret CMK, distinct from content and from every other table (R-SECRETS). Application-layer AEAD is the real protection; SSE is defence in depth.

stream.rationale: Disabled deliberately: no consumer role should ever be able to read secret ciphertext off a change feed, and there is no legitimate regional consumer.

timeToLive.rationale: Deletion is explicit, so TTL would only create a silent erasure path for secret material.

tables.purpose: The provider-mandated hierarchical branch-key store. Key attribute names are branch-key-id and type because the AWS Encryption SDK hierarchical keyring defines them; this is the one table that does not use the pk and sk convention, and the deviation is deliberate. The logical key store name equals the physical table name and is cryptographically bound to every record, so it can never be changed after first use.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Deleting this table permanently destroys every workspace secret, so it carries its own CMK and its own deletion protection.

stream.rationale: Wrapped branch-key material must never appear on a change feed.

timeToLive.rationale: A branch key is decryptable material for every ciphertext ever sealed under it; expiry by TTL would silently destroy customer secrets.

tables.purpose: Durable runnable work: wake, due, claim, lease, fence, attempt, dedupe claims and per-shard reconciliation cursors over one sharded due index. Also carries the transactional usage-fact outbox so usage workers need no content or session visibility.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Per-authority customer managed key; the work table never holds customer content, only typed non-content work metadata.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_due
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Sixty-four shards, never a literal single due partition. The index attributes are removed when work reaches done or poisoned, so the index holds only outstanding work. Priority is folded into effectiveDueAt as a lead, which gives priority ordering plus bounded ageing with one sort key.

stream.rationale: NEW_IMAGE is safe only because the codec rejects a payload map larger than 4 KiB or carrying a key outside the declared per-kind schema, which keeps non-content work metadata only an enforced property rather than an assumed one.

timeToLive.rationale: Set to updatedAt plus 24 hours when a record reaches done. A redelivered hint inside the window finds state done and acks; after it, the domain re-derives a no-op. Both arms are correct, so TTL timing is not a fence.

tables.purpose: The exact Hands generation head, lifecycle intents and immutable receipts, transactional usage outbox, true-idle probes, the current-generation pointer a Brain activation reads, and a sharded evaluation due index for the reaper.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Per-authority customer managed key. The table holds generation metadata only, never customer content.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_runtime_due
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Sixteen shards over generation heads and undelivered usage outbox rows. A dedicated due index avoids one work-item rewrite per generation per evaluation and keeps receipt delivery retryable after a terminal head leaves the index.

stream.rationale: The table holds no customer content, only generation metadata, so NEW_IMAGE is safe and gives the worker a state-change hint without a read.

timeToLive.rationale: Probes only, at 7 days. Receipts have no TTL: they are lifecycle evidence referenced by usage facts.

tables.purpose: Session heads, messages, runs, native events, approvals, agent control and journals, durable operations, idempotency receipts, and the fenced empty-workspace control row. Brain session-level items live here under the BRAIN# sort-key prefix; per-agent items get their own partition.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Per-authority customer managed key; content and secret authorities use different keys (R-SECRETS).

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_workspace_index
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Only session heads and operation states carry the index attributes, so a list query can never surface a prompt, a journal entry or an idempotency receipt. lifecycle sits inside the index partition key so trash moves the item and purge removes it entirely, which makes ordinary list filter-free.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_workspace_events
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Only native events carry these attributes. Hour partitions prevent a hot unbounded workspace feed and the session and observation tie-breakers make cross-session ordering total.

stream.rationale: Least privilege: the stream consumer role learns pk and sk and nothing else. Replay and ordering are always Query by cursor; the stream is never truth.

timeToLive.rationale: Space reclamation only (OD-16, 24 hours). Every TTL'd row also carries an explicit expiresAt the reader checks; no fence reads TTL.

tables.purpose: Immutable compute.millicpu_ms.v1 and memory.byte_ms.v1 usage facts plus the zero-dollar model-token, provider-call and tool-invocation observability facts, their identity claims, frontier, outbox, receipts, correction heads, quarantine markers, the run and operation closure vectors and the mux activation crash-recovery cursor. The meter attribute is the discriminator; a storage or transfer meter is refused before any write and again on read.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Billing evidence and customer content are different blast radii, so the usage authorities never share the content or secret key; one key per authority keeps a category compromise from reaching a sibling.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_fact_id
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: A settlement receipt carries only region, category and factId, so it needs a way back to the workspace partition. Only the ID# claim carries factId as a key attribute, which is also why the claim is a separate item: a GSI cannot be condition-checked and the admission fence has to be a condition. itemType is projected because an INCLUDE projection carries no discriminator of its own, and a row decoded without one is a row decoded as the wrong shape.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_outbox_due
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Sixteen shards over an enqueue-instant then sequence ordering, so the sweep reads the oldest undelivered facts first with a bounded page per shard. The index attributes exist only on a pending OUTBOX# row, so a confirmed SendMessage removes the row and with it the index entry.

stream.rationale: NEW_IMAGE is safe here because a fact row holds integers, identifiers and receipt references only: never customer content, never a prompt, never a secret. An observability fact carries token counts and a model identifier, which are already public in the customer's own usage view. The event-source mapping filters itemType = usage_fact on INSERT.

timeToLive.rationale: Every row in an authority table is money evidence. A fact that silently expired would be an unrecoverable accounting gap, so the only TTL in this stream is on rebuildable usage-query-projection detail rows.

tables.purpose: Rebuildable, generation-keyed customer usage read model: hourly and daily aggregates over the declared dimension tuple, bounded detail rows, the copied coverage vector and the generation pointer. It is not charge truth and may be dropped and rebuilt from the authority facts plus the settlement receipts at any time, which is exactly why it is the one table in this stream that may expire a row.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: The projection is customer-readable and holds no provider evidence, but it still derives from billing data, so it stays on a usage-owned key rather than on a content or secret key.

stream.rationale: The projection is derived state. Anything that wanted to react to a usage change reacts to the authority stream instead, so a rebuild writing generation n+1 never produces a fan-out storm of derived events.

timeToLive.rationale: Detail rows are a ninety-day convenience over facts that remain in the authority forever, so expiring one loses nothing recoverable. TTL is never the fence: every detail row also carries an explicit expiresAt string that the reader checks, so a late deletion cannot serve a row the reader should already refuse.

tables.purpose: Immutable storage.byte_min.v1 usage facts, their deterministic identity claims, the four-stage frontier, the central settlement outbox, settlement receipts, correction heads, quarantine markers and the durable minute accrual cursor. Every row is money evidence, so nothing here is ever updated in place except the frontier and the revision-fenced cursor, and nothing is ever deleted except a delivered outbox marker.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Billing evidence and customer content are different blast radii, so the usage authorities never share the content or secret key; one key per authority keeps a category compromise from reaching a sibling.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_fact_id
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: A settlement receipt carries only region, category and factId, so it needs a way back to the workspace partition. Only the ID# claim carries factId as a key attribute, which is also why the claim is a separate item: a GSI cannot be condition-checked and the admission fence has to be a condition. itemType is projected because an INCLUDE projection carries no discriminator of its own, and a row decoded without one is a row decoded as the wrong shape.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_outbox_due
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Sixteen shards over an enqueue-instant then sequence ordering, so the sweep reads the oldest undelivered facts first with a bounded page per shard. The index attributes exist only on a pending OUTBOX# row, so a confirmed SendMessage removes the row and with it the index entry.

stream.rationale: NEW_IMAGE is safe here because a fact row holds integers, identifiers and receipt references only: never customer content, never a prompt, never a secret. Carrying the whole fact is what lets the worker project without reading the table back. The event-source mapping filters itemType = usage_fact on INSERT, so frontier, outbox, cursor and receipt writes never wake the worker.

timeToLive.rationale: Every row in an authority table is money evidence. A fact that silently expired would be an unrecoverable accounting gap, so the only TTL in this stream is on rebuildable usage-query-projection detail rows.

tables.purpose: Immutable data_transfer.egress_byte.v1 usage facts, their identity claims, frontier, outbox, receipts, correction heads, quarantine markers and the one-crossing-one-fact claim that keeps two adapters counting the same physical write from both producing a fact. Counter-mode and receipt-mode evidence stay distinct and are never merged.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Billing evidence and customer content are different blast radii, so the usage authorities never share the content or secret key; one key per authority keeps a category compromise from reaching a sibling.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_fact_id
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: A settlement receipt carries only region, category and factId, so it needs a way back to the workspace partition. Only the ID# claim carries factId as a key attribute, which is also why the claim is a separate item: a GSI cannot be condition-checked and the admission fence has to be a condition. itemType is projected because an INCLUDE projection carries no discriminator of its own, and a row decoded without one is a row decoded as the wrong shape.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_outbox_due
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: Sixteen shards over an enqueue-instant then sequence ordering, so the sweep reads the oldest undelivered facts first with a bounded page per shard. The index attributes exist only on a pending OUTBOX# row, so a confirmed SendMessage removes the row and with it the index entry.

stream.rationale: NEW_IMAGE is safe here because a fact row holds integers, identifiers and receipt references only: a byte count and a boundary name, never the bytes themselves and never a URL. The event-source mapping filters itemType = usage_fact on INSERT.

timeToLive.rationale: Every row in an authority table is money evidence. A crossing claim that silently expired would let the same physical crossing be billed twice, which is the one direction this table must never fail.
